channel.title: AlphaGen Research
channel.description: AlphaGen Notes and briefs on debt, equities, and macro.

item.title: Aerospace and defense: backlogs are growing faster than sales
item.description: RTX, GE Aerospace and Northrop Grumman all raised 2026 guidance on Oct. 20, and all three are booking demand faster than they can ship it.

item.title: Fed plumbing: Treasury's cash account, not QT, is now moving reserves
item.description: With the Fed's balance sheet flat and its reverse repo facility nearly empty, swings in Treasury's cash balance are passing straight through to bank reserves.

item.title: Morning Brief: Regional banks split between clean beats and balance-sheet resets
item.description: Truist takes a $1.4 billion securities loss and sells RAC loans while Citizens, Regions and M&T post cleaner quarters; import prices and industrial production follow, and Europe confirms 3.8% inflation.

item.title: The Close: Strong top lines, uneven margins from brokers to freight
item.description: Interactive Brokers, J.B. Hunt and Alcoa capped a heavy reporting day, while the Fed's H.15 shows the 2-year yield rising as the long end eased.

item.title: Crop protection's reset: FMC reprices the channel as Corteva fights in court
item.description: FMC's guidance cut and Corteva's legal fight over its split show the crop-input business working through price deflation and governance risk at the same time.

item.title: Beyond the banks: margins, warehouses and temp workers point to a sturdier real economy
item.description: UnitedHealth, Prologis and ManpowerGroup add non-financial evidence to a week dominated by bank results and an energy-driven inflation shock.

item.title: September PPI: the energy shock moves up the pipeline
item.description: Producer prices posted their biggest monthly gain since March 2022, and upstream costs are rising far faster than consumer core inflation.

item.title: Morning Brief: Producer prices and retail sales test the energy shock
item.description: September PPI and retail sales land together at 8:30 a.m., with a delayed EIA oil inventory report, Freddie Mac mortgage rates and two bill auctions to follow.

item.title: Beige Book: the oil shock is everywhere, demand is not
item.description: Every District reported higher oil prices feeding costs, while consumer spending was flat and growth mostly slight. That mix shapes the pace of the Fed's tightening.

item.title: Fannie Mae's new forecast pushes mortgage relief past 2027
item.description: One month after projecting rates near 6.7%, Fannie Mae's economists now see 7.5% next year and fewer home sales.

item.title: EIA's October outlook: oil supply is healing, inventories are not
item.description: The Energy Information Administration sees Brent easing from a $114 September to $105 in the fourth quarter, but its own numbers show global stocks still drawing and diesel still tight.

item.title: The Close: Bank earnings show growth, with credit and compliance bills attached
item.description: Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, State Street and BlackRock all grew revenue in the third quarter, while the Fed's H.15 shows long Treasury yields easing off last week's levels.

item.title: Q3 financials: fee engines are carrying the quarter
item.description: BlackRock and State Street posted double-digit revenue growth on market-linked fees, while Bank of America and Wells Fargo show balance-sheet banks paying for compliance and building reserves.

item.title: September CPI: an energy shock, not a broad reacceleration
item.description: Headline inflation jumped to 3.7% on gasoline, while core held at 2.6%. The gap between the two is now the central question for the Fed on October 28.
